title: PAH-OMC-020 projective local-correlation word envelope
question: Can the unchanged PAH-001 grade-blind eventual intertwining and the registered R-515-R-517 word controls yield a scalar n-Cauchy envelope for one non-radial local cylinder without assuming a common U_n?
finding: Conditionally yes for a finite word truncation. R-493 identifies every retained word after the support-dependent stabilization stage. R-510 supplies the local Gibbs-state passage for the product cylinder, while R-516 and R-517 give b=144 and the explicit two-copy b_eff=288 factorial boundary tail. The resulting scalar envelope decreases in the n and boundary-distance fixtures. This does not identify the envelope with the R-512 minimal semigroup or prove the full anchored-n limit.
decision_reason: This is a distinct projective comparison step rather than another finite carrier table. The finite cutoff makes the use of R-493 exact, and the two-copy factor and factorial remainder are exposed rather than hidden. Independent arithmetic, hostile shortcut rejection and Lean finite checks all pass. The result remains conditional because the common varying-space realization and minimal-form identification are absent.
boundary: Exact PAH-001 functional, OMC-013 grade-blind cylinder, R-510 local state and R-515-R-517 post-j finite-fibre controls. No new rate, state, carrier, projection, counterterm, time interpretation or limit order.
